label: a6-049-cor-monotone-converges-iff-bounded
tail:
No fatal mathematical defects found in the proof. The forward direction is exactly the cited lemma; the converse correctly reduces boundedness (absolute‑value form) to the one‑sided bounds required by the monotone convergence theorem, and the case split is exhaustive. Two remarks contain claims about other library items that cannot be verified from the given dependencies and may be false.

### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: Remarks, paragraph "This is the form in which the result is used."
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "Bolzano-Weierstrass ([[thm-bolzano-weierstrass]]) extracts a monotone subsequence of a bounded sequence and then needs exactly this corollary, since what is available about the subsequence is boundedness, inherited from the sequence, and not a bound on a particular side."
WHY IT FAILS: The claim describes the proof of another item (thm-bolzano-weierstrass) which is not among the dependencies provided for review. The auditor cannot verify that this description is accurate; it could be a false statement about how that theorem is proved. In the context of this audit, the truth of this remark is unverified and potentially false, which undermines the page's accuracy.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Either remove the remark, include the relevant item so it can be verified, or rephrase to avoid specific unverifiable claims about other items.

### FINDING 2 — NONFATAL — location: Remarks, paragraph "Neither hypothesis can be dropped."
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "Without monotonicity the converse direction fails, by [[fs-bounded-implies-convergent]]. Without boundedness the forward direction is what fails, and it fails in the describable way recorded by [[lem-monotone-unbounded-diverges]]: a nondecreasing unbounded sequence diverges to $+\infty$."
WHY IT FAILS: These claims cite two items (fs-bounded-implies-convergent and lem-monotone-unbounded-diverges) that are not provided. The assertions about the existence of counterexamples and the behavior of unbounded monotone sequences are attributed to these specific library items, and without them we cannot confirm that the cited items indeed support the claims as stated. The page therefore contains unverifiable statements.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Provide the referenced items so the claims can be checked, or rephrase the remarks to stand on their own without relying on unverified library items.
